Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class PacketBoundaryChecks

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.PacketBoundaryChecks
public final class PacketBoundaryChecks extends Object
The shared packet boundary and the mutation handlers behind it: accepted entry-point dispatch, gesture pacing, held-item requirements, cell bounds, and refused extraction states.

Each test is handed a playerFactory that builds a fake player holding the given main hand item; the loader shell supplies it, since obtaining a fake player is loader-native.

      public static void extractIgnoresAnEmptyCell(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Function<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack,net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer> playerFactory)
      Extraction is the one mutation packet that acts on a cell the client chose rather than one the server recomputes, so the per-type handler checks are what stand between a client integer and the stored contents. The extraction tests below drive those handlers directly with an index or a hand the gesture could never have produced.

    • refusedBarExtractionLeavesTheBlockStanding

      public static void refusedBarExtractionLeavesTheBlockStanding(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Function<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack,net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer> playerFactory)
      A refused Bar extraction must also leave the support cascade unrun. Taking the bar would empty the block, which removes itself and drops what it held, so the block still standing with its bar in place is the whole of the guarantee.
